main_question: Could simple metadata explain the task?
rationale: A sanity baseline was needed before acoustic representation work so the study could detect whether trivial recording-duration signals dominated.
key_result: Provisional local labeled test ROC-AUC 0.4437.
significance: Indicated that metadata alone was insufficient and should not be the main modeling route.
main_limitation: Provisional local labeled test was not official hidden AVEC evaluation.
next_step_motivated: Test learned speech representations rather than metadata only.

model_or_feature_set: WavLM base-plus final layer, participant mean
main_question: Did a default final WavLM layer provide a usable baseline?
rationale: The first WavLM baseline established whether frozen SSL speech embeddings were worth optimizing before layer and aggregation analysis.
key_result: Provisional local labeled test ROC-AUC 0.5195; development ROC-AUC 0.5692.
significance: Suggested that final-layer WavLM was weak and motivated inspecting intermediate layers.
main_limitation: Provisional local labeled test was not official hidden AVEC evaluation.
next_step_motivated: Run layer-wise WavLM analysis on DAIC training data.

classifier_or_protocol: Train-only nested repeated stratified CV with logistic regression
main_question: Which frozen WavLM layer should be carried forward?
rationale: Layer choice can change downstream performance, so selection was done before Android evaluation using DAIC development data only.
key_result: Layer 9 was selected; train-only mean outer ROC-AUC 0.5956 and registry paper-ready ROC-AUC 0.6443 under recorded train/development protocol.
significance: Provided the frozen representation layer for later free-speech-compatible transfer tests.
main_limitation: Ablation supported method selection only within DAIC-WOZ development data.
next_step_motivated: Test participant aggregation strategies for layer 9.

classifier_or_protocol: Mean, median, and mean plus standard deviation PCA participant aggregation
main_question: How should window-level WavLM embeddings become participant-level features?
rationale: The study needed a participant-level representation before participant-level classification and transfer.
key_result: Mean aggregation retained ROC-AUC 0.5956 in the results table; median was 0.5905 and mean plus std PCA was 0.5683.
significance: Supported a simple participant mean as the frozen aggregation method.
main_limitation: Aggregation was not the main bottleneck and was still DAIC-only method selection.
next_step_motivated: Compare WavLM with guided-interview timing features.

speech_task: guided interview timing and participant speech
model_or_feature_set: Timing features and WavLM layer-9 embeddings
classifier_or_protocol: Timing-only, WavLM-only, and early-fusion logistic regression
main_question: Did guided-interview timing add signal beyond frozen WavLM?
rationale: Timing features were evaluated because DAIC-WOZ includes interaction structure that may reflect response latency and speaking dynamics.
key_result: Timing-only reached train nested-CV ROC-AUC 0.6126; WavLM-only was 0.5956; early fusion was 0.5747.
significance: Indicated useful DAIC guided-interview timing signal but did not make timing portable to Android.
main_limitation: Timing features depended on DAIC guided-interview structure and were not directly Android-compatible.
next_step_motivated: Evaluate safer late fusion without leaking test information.

speech_task: guided interview timing and participant speech
model_or_feature_set: Timing model plus WavLM model scores
classifier_or_protocol: Timing-only, WavLM-only, weighted late fusion, and logistic stacking
main_question: Could late fusion improve over the best single DAIC candidate?
rationale: Late fusion tested whether complementary WavLM and timing signals could be combined after separate model estimation.
key_result: Timing-only remained strongest at ROC-AUC 0.6245 in registry paper-ready interpretation; weighted late fusion was 0.6044 and logistic stacking was 0.5413 in results table.
significance: Supported retaining timing-only as the DAIC guided-interview candidate and WavLM as the transfer-compatible candidate.
main_limitation: Fusion did not improve reliability and timing still lacked Android compatibility.
next_step_motivated: Freeze final DAIC candidates for one provisional local labeled test evaluation.

classifier_or_protocol: Balanced logistic regression with frozen Candidate A threshold
main_question: How did the transfer-compatible WavLM candidate perform on the local DAIC test?
rationale: A frozen WavLM candidate was needed for later cross-corpus application because timing features could not be assumed in Android.
key_result: Provisional local labeled test ROC-AUC 0.5065; frozen Candidate A threshold 0.5558.
significance: Although weak on DAIC local test, it remained the only free-speech-compatible DAIC candidate for Android transfer.
main_limitation: Local test provenance was provisional and not official hidden AVEC; no post-test model changes were permitted.
next_step_motivated: Use Candidate A for Android zero-shot transfer.

classifier_or_protocol: Balanced logistic regression with frozen Candidate B threshold
main_question: How did the best DAIC timing candidate perform on the local DAIC test?
rationale: The timing candidate tested whether guided-interview interaction features were stronger than WavLM inside DAIC conditions.
key_result: Provisional local labeled test ROC-AUC 0.6775; selected C 100.0; frozen threshold 0.2927.
significance: Showed that timing features were useful inside DAIC guided interviews.
main_limitation: Timing definitions did not transfer directly to Android because compatible response-latency features were unavailable.
next_step_motivated: Perform Android audit before attempting transfer.

model_or_feature_set: corpus inventory and WavLM preprocessing audit
main_question: Could Androids Corpus support DAIC-to-Android transfer and within-Android task analysis?
rationale: The study needed to verify participants, tasks, labels, and feature compatibility before any Android modeling.
key_result: Android inventory recorded 118 participants, 116 interviews, 112 readings, 874 interview clips, and reproducible WavLM preprocessing; timing direct transfer was invalid.
significance: Established which Android protocols were scientifically permissible.
main_limitation: This was an audit, not classifier evaluation.
next_step_motivated: Apply frozen DAIC WavLM to Android interview speech.

classifier_or_protocol: Frozen DAIC logistic regression applied without Android fitting
main_question: Does the complete DAIC-trained WavLM classifier transfer directly to Android interview speech?
rationale: Zero-shot testing had to come before adaptation to separate direct model transfer from target-domain fitting.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.6412, PR-AUC 0.6809, Brier 0.4056; both 0.5 and frozen DAIC thresholds predicted all Android participants negative.
significance: Indicated limited cross-corpus ranking transfer but failed thresholded classification.
main_limitation: Different language, corpus, label definition, and probability scale limited direct transfer.
next_step_motivated: Diagnose threshold shift, calibration shift, and classifier-boundary shift in Phase 2C.

experiment_name: Protocol A frozen DAIC zero-shot reference
classifier_or_protocol: Protocol A: no Android fitting or adaptation
main_question: Can Phase 2B zero-shot ranking be reproduced as the fixed reference?
rationale: A fixed reference was needed so adaptation and Android-trained protocols could be compared against the same frozen score generator.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.6412.
significance: Anchored all Phase 2C comparisons to the unchanged DAIC score ranking.
main_limitation: Still produced all-negative thresholded predictions at frozen thresholds.
next_step_motivated: Evaluate target-domain threshold adaptation without changing the score ranking.

training_domain: Frozen DAIC scores plus Android training-fold thresholds
classifier_or_protocol: Protocol B: threshold adapted using target training folds
main_question: Was failure partly an operating-threshold problem?
rationale: Threshold adaptation tested whether decision rules could be shifted without learning a new Android classifier.
key_result: ROC-AUC remained 0.6412; macro F1 improved to 0.5688 and balanced accuracy to 0.5733.
significance: Supported the interpretation that threshold shift contributed to transfer failure.
main_limitation: It used Android labels and therefore was not pure zero-shot evaluation.
next_step_motivated: Evaluate frozen-score calibration as a probability-scale diagnosis.

training_domain: Frozen DAIC scores plus Android training-fold calibration
main_question: Did target-domain calibration repair probability scale or ranking?
rationale: Calibration was separated from thresholding because probability quality and rank discrimination answer different questions.
key_result: Brier score improved to 0.2474, but ROC-AUC decreased to 0.5694.
significance: Indicated that calibration improved probability scale under folds but did not improve ranking transfer.
main_limitation: It used Android labels and was not pure zero-shot evaluation.
next_step_motivated: Train an Android-specific classifier boundary using the same frozen representation.

main_question: Can the frozen representation support an Android-specific decision boundary?
rationale: Training on Android labels tested whether the representation retained useful information even when the DAIC classifier boundary failed.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.8675, PR-AUC 0.8892, Brier 0.1695, balanced accuracy 0.8275, macro F1 0.8263.
significance: Provided evidence for representation usefulness with a target-domain classifier boundary.
main_limitation: This was within-Android cross-validation, not DAIC-to-Android transfer or external validation.
next_step_motivated: Compare Android reading speech and task effects.

main_question: What changed between DAIC and Android beyond threshold choice?
rationale: Domain-shift analysis was needed to explain why ranking partly transferred while thresholded classification failed.
key_result: DAIC-to-Android centroid cosine distance 0.1767, mean absolute standardized shift 2.3116, and 550 of 768 features shifted more than one DAIC SD.
significance: Supported the classifier-boundary and distribution-shift interpretation.
main_limitation: Descriptive shift statistics do not identify a causal mechanism.
next_step_motivated: Evaluate reading speech and within-Android task transfer.

classifier_or_protocol: Frozen DAIC classifier applied without Android reading fitting
main_question: Does direct DAIC transfer also fail on reading speech?
rationale: Reading zero-shot tested whether transfer behavior depended on the Android speech task.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.5795, PR-AUC 0.5997, Brier 0.3351; thresholded predictions were all negative.
significance: Showed modest ranking signal but failed thresholded classification, matching the interview transfer pattern.
main_limitation: It was cross-corpus zero-shot only, not an Android-trained result.
next_step_motivated: Train an Android reading classifier using the same representation.

main_question: Can the same representation support within-Android reading classification?
rationale: Reading evaluation tested whether controlled read speech carried depression-related signal under Android labels.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.8796 with 95 percent CI [0.8113, 0.9377], PR-AUC 0.8929, Brier 0.1438.
significance: Provided a within-Android reading benchmark comparable to the interview benchmark.
main_limitation: It was within-corpus validation, not external validation.
next_step_motivated: Compare reading and interview tasks descriptively and then with participant-coherent folds.

main_question: Were reading and interview task representations broadly similar?
rationale: A task comparison was needed before controlled cross-task transfer, but Phase 2D folds were not participant-coherent across tasks.
key_result: Task centroid cosine distance was 0.0442, within-participant task cosine similarity was 0.9273, and 292 of 768 features shifted more than one interview SD.
significance: Suggested overlap between task representations while preserving evidence of task shift.
main_limitation: The comparison was descriptive and did not replace participant-coherent cross-task testing.
next_step_motivated: Run Phase 2E participant-coherent cross-task transfer.

main_question: What is the within-task reading reference under paired-participant folds?
rationale: Matched-task references were needed so cross-task transfer gaps used the same participant-coherent fold design.
significance: Established the reading reference for cross-task comparisons.
main_limitation: Within-Android estimate only; not external validation.
next_step_motivated: Compare interview-to-reading transfer against matched reading.

main_question: What is the within-task interview reference under paired-participant folds?
rationale: Matched interview reference was needed to measure reading-to-interview transfer loss.
significance: Established the interview reference for cross-task comparisons.
main_limitation: Within-Android estimate only; not external validation.
next_step_motivated: Compare reading-to-interview transfer against matched interview.

main_question: Does a classifier trained on reading speech transfer to interview speech from held-out participants?
rationale: This tested whether task-invariant representation information survived a classifier boundary learned on the other task.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.8475; gap versus matched interview -0.0590 with interval [-0.1316, 0.0116].
significance: Supported shared but task-sensitive information across reading and interview speech.
main_limitation: Transfer remained below the matched interview point estimate and was within Androids Corpus only.
next_step_motivated: Evaluate the reverse transfer direction and pooled-task training.

main_question: Does a classifier trained on interview speech transfer to reading speech from held-out participants?
rationale: The reverse direction tested whether cross-task transfer was symmetric enough to support shared representation claims.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.8501; gap versus matched reading -0.0547 with interval [-0.1436, 0.0325].
significance: Supported cross-task sharing while preserving task-specific boundary limitations.
main_limitation: Transfer remained below the matched reading point estimate and was within Androids Corpus only.
next_step_motivated: Evaluate pooled reading/interview training.

speech_task: pooled reading plus interview to reading
main_question: Does exposure to both tasks improve reading evaluation?
rationale: Pooled training tested whether combining task examples could stabilize the classifier boundary.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.9058; gain over interview-to-reading 0.0557 with CI [-0.0172, 0.1340].
significance: Produced the strongest reading point estimate, but the gain interval included zero.
main_limitation: Within-corpus pooled-task estimate only; not definitive superiority.
next_step_motivated: Evaluate pooled-to-interview and boundary similarity.

speech_task: pooled reading plus interview to interview
main_question: Does exposure to both tasks improve interview evaluation?
rationale: The pooled-to-interview test checked whether multi-task exposure also helped the less constrained speech task.
key_result: ROC-AUC 0.9135; gain over reading-to-interview 0.0660 with CI [-0.0013, 0.1346].
significance: Produced the strongest interview point estimate, but the gain interval included zero.
main_limitation: Within-corpus pooled-task estimate only; not definitive superiority.
next_step_motivated: Summarize classifier-boundary and score-similarity diagnostics.

main_question: How similar were the task-specific classifier boundaries?
rationale: Boundary analysis helped explain why cross-task transfer worked but did not fully match within-task models.
key_result: Coefficient cosine similarity 0.4752, sign agreement 0.6659, top-50 Jaccard 0.1216, matched score correlation 0.7123, cross-target score correlation 0.5555.
significance: Supported the claim of shared representation information with task-sensitive classifier boundaries.
main_limitation: Coefficient comparisons are descriptive and not causal feature importance.
next_step_motivated: Frame final interpretation cautiously in BSPC manuscript.
